question.text: Will the InfoGripe bulletin for epidemiological week 46 of 2026 report a national growth trend in COVID-19 SRAG hospitalisations?
question.resolution_criteria: InfoGripe's weekly "Resumo do Boletim InfoGripe" for epidemiological week 46 of 2026 (header "Semana Epidemiológica (SE) 46 2026"; week of 15–21 November 2026) is expected to be published by Agência Fiocruz de Notícias on Thursday 26 November 2026 and is linked from https://agencia.fiocruz.br/ ; the previous edition, in the same series and format, is https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_44-1.pdf . This question resolves YES if the national-level summary text of that edition (its "Pontos de destaque nesta atualização" highlights list and/or its "Situação nacional" section) states that, in Brazil as a whole, SRAG hospitalisations confirmed for COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2) show growth — wording such as "sinal de crescimento" or "crescimento" applied to COVID-19 SRAG / "casos graves por Covid-19" at the national level, for either the long-term (last 6 weeks) or the short-term (last 3 weeks) trend. It resolves NO if that text describes national COVID-19 SRAG only as stable or oscillating ("estabilização", "oscilação"), falling ("queda"), decelerating, or having stopped growing ("desaceleração do crescimento", "interrupção do crescimento", "fim do crescimento"), or makes no statement of national growth in COVID-19 SRAG.
question.fine_print: Growth in either the long-term (6-week) or the short-term (3-week) trend is sufficient for YES; it is not required that both horizons show growth. Growth statements that concern only particular states, regions or capitals do not count, nor does a statement of growth confined to specific age groups with no statement of growth for the national aggregate as a whole. A statement of growth in COVID-19 SRAG deaths without any growth statement about COVID-19 SRAG cases/hospitalisations does not count as YES. If no Resumo do Boletim InfoGripe covering epidemiological week 46 of 2026 has been published by 23:59 UTC on 27 November 2026, the question is annulled.

research:
The latest InfoGripe edition (SE 44, released 12 November 2026) still reports a national growth signal for COVID-19 SRAG, and nothing published so far settles the SE 46 outcome. I could not read the text of the resolution PDF itself (both PDF fetches returned unreadable binary), so the SE 44 wording below comes from the Agência Fiocruz article about that edition.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-12: The SE 44 edition (data for 1-7 November) says "há um sinal de crescimento do número de casos confirmados de SRAG por Covid-19" and that severe COVID-19 cases "permanece[m] em níveis baixos no país". The article does not say whether this is the long-term or short-term trend. Overall SRAG is falling on both horizons. SARS-CoV-2 was 11.5% of positive cases and 26.9% of positive deaths in the last 4 weeks. Mato Grosso already shows "desaceleração do crescimento". [Agência Fiocruz](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/infogripe-aponta-aumento-do-numero-de-casos-de-covid-19)
- I could not get the underlying InfoGripe data: the Fiocruz GitLab repository asks for a login.
- 2026-11-16: The Agência Fiocruz homepage shows no InfoGripe item newer than 12 November. [Agência Fiocruz](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The SE 45 edition is expected around 19 November and SE 46 around 26 November.
- The national COVID-19 SRAG growth signal has appeared in at least two editions in a row (SE 43 and SE 44).
- The COVID-19 share of positive cases rose from 8.5% (SE 43) to 11.5% (SE 44), and the number of states named with growth went from 5 to 6.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-14/15: Press coverage repeats the SE 44 findings: COVID-19 SRAG rising in DF, MG, SP, RJ, PR and BA. Fiocruz calls the situation "not yet worrying". [Exame](https://exame.com/brasil/casos-graves-de-covid-19-voltam-a-crescer-no-brasil-veja-quem-pode-se-vacinar-pelo-sus/), [ISTOÉ](https://istoe.com.br/covid-19-fiocruz-alta-casos-graves-seis-estados)
- 2026-11-14: According to a news report citing the Ministry of Health, the XFG subvariant makes up about 90% of sequenced cases, with mild cases rising in 17 states plus DF. [UOL](https://www.uol.com.br/vivabem/noticias/redacao/2026/11/14/xfg-o-que-se-sabe-sobre-a-variante-do-coronavirus-que-circula-no-brasil.ghtm)
- 2026-11-12: SE 44 edition published (details in section 1). [Agência Fiocruz](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/infogripe-aponta-aumento-do-numero-de-casos-de-covid-19)
- 2026-11-10: Ministry of Health (data to 31 October):
  - Mild COVID-19 cases are trending up in 18 states over the last 6 weeks.
  - COVID-19 SRAG is growing in MT, DF, RJ, SP and SC, all at low levels.
  - 2026 totals: about 3,400 SRAG cases (63% below 2025) and 437 deaths (69% below).
  - The ministry says end-of-year increases are expected, as in previous years. [gov.br](https://www.gov.br/saude/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/2026/novembro/covid-19-casos-e-obitos-seguem-em-queda-no-brasil)
- 2026-11-05: The SE 43 edition reports national SRAG growth from metapneumovirus, rhinovirus and COVID-19. COVID-19 was 8.5% of positive cases and 24.1% of positive deaths, with growth in MT, DF, SP, RJ and SC, all at very low incidence. [Fiocruz](https://fiocruz.br/noticia/2026/11/infogripe-cresce-o-numero-de-casos-de-srag-por-metapneumovirus-rinovirus-e-covid-19)
- Early October 2026 (unverified): One search summary mentioned an 8 October bulletin showing SARS-CoV-2 increases. I could not confirm that it refers to 2026.
- A Ministry of Health SE 42 report (data to 24 October) reportedly describes "leve crescimento" of COVID-19. I could not read the PDF to check. [gov.br SE 42](https://www.gov.br/saude/pt-br/assuntos/saude-de-a-a-z/c/covid-19/publicacoes-tecnicas/informes/informe-sindromes-gripais-se-42-de-2026.pdf)

## 4. Base rates
- I could not find a systematic count of how long InfoGripe's national COVID-19 growth signals last. Older Resumo PDFs exist (for example [2024 SE 36](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/u91/resumo_infogripe_2024_36.pdf) and [2025 SE 09](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2025_09.pdf)), but I did not tally them.
- What is known:
  - The signal has been present for at least 2 editions in a row (SE 43 and 44), possibly longer.
  - The rise in mild cases (which tends to come before hospitalisations) is broad, across 18 states, and an XFG wave is under way.
  - The first signs of slowing are local only: Mato Grosso, the state that led the rise, now shows "desaceleração".
  - Weekly national COVID-19 SRAG counts are small, a few hundred, so the signal can tip into "estabilização" from noise.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets relate to InfoGripe or Brazilian COVID-19 trends. I found no expert or model forecast for this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- ~2026-11-17/18: Ministry of Health "Informe Síndromes Gripais" for SE 44/45.
- ~2026-11-19 (Thursday): InfoGripe SE 45 edition, the most direct lead indicator. Watch for any wording like "desaceleração", "interrupção" or "estabilização" for national COVID-19.
- ~2026-11-26 (Thursday): InfoGripe SE 46 edition, which decides the question. It is annulled if not published by 23:59 UTC on 27 November.

Other sources: [Forbes Brasil](https://forbes.com.br/forbes-saude/2026/11/ministerio-da-saude-alerta-para-alta-de-covid-19-em-18-estados/), [Medicina S/A](https://medicinasa.com.br/aumento-casos-covid-2026/), [Diário de Pernambuco](https://www.diariodepernambuco.com.br/brasil/2026/11/11728591-covid-19-pelo-menos-5-estados-registram-aumento-de-casos-graves.html), [Revista Fórum](https://revistaforum.com.br/saude/fiocruz-alta-casos-graves-covid-19/)

## 4. Base rates
- I could not find a systematic count of how long InfoGripe's national COVID-19 growth signals usually last.
- The current national signal has appeared in at least two straight editions (SE 43 and SE 44). I could not confirm whether the SE 41 or SE 42 editions also carried it.
- The leading indicators all pointed up as of SE 44: positivity rising for about nine weeks, mild cases rising in 18 or more states, and COVID's share of positive SRAG climbing. Hospitalisations normally lag infections, which tends to support persistence.
- Signs pointing the other way:
  - Mato Grosso, which led the rise, is already decelerating.
  - Weekly national COVID-19 SRAG counts are small.
  - The bulletin's wording can switch to "estabilização" once the most recent weeks flatten, especially after nowcasting.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain. The SE 46 Resumo is due Thursday 26 November 2026. For YES, its national highlights or "Situação nacional" section must say that COVID-19 SRAG shows growth ("sinal de crescimento") nationally, on either the 6-week or the 3-week trend.

(b) Status quo: the last two editions (SE 43 and SE 44) both reported national COVID-19 SRAG growth. If nothing changes, the answer is YES.

(c) Base rate: once InfoGripe declares a national COVID-19 SRAG growth signal during an emerging wave, the signal usually lasts several editions, often 4 to 8 weeks. The 6-week long-term trend is especially sticky. Given a signal in two consecutive editions with rising leading indicators, I estimate it is still present two editions later about 70-75% of the time.

(d) Evidence:
- For YES:
  - SE 43 (5 November) and SE 44 (12 November) both report national growth.
  - The COVID share of positive SRAG cases rose from 8.5% to 11.5%.
  - The number of states with rising COVID SRAG went from 5 to 6.
  - ITpS test positivity was about 17% around SE 44, the highest since February and still climbing, after roughly nine weeks of rises.
  - Mild cases are rising in 18 states.
  - XFG makes up about 90% of sequenced cases.
  - Hospitalisations lag infections.
- For NO:
  - Mato Grosso, the state that led the rise, already shows "desaceleração".
  - National weekly counts are small, a few hundred.
  - Nowcasting of recent weeks can flatten the trend into "estabilização".
  - The summary might mention growth only for states.

(e) Scenarios:
- NO: positivity peaks around mid-November, SE 45 reports "desaceleração", and SE 46 describes national COVID SRAG as stabilising or oscillating.
- YES: the XFG wave keeps spreading to the Southeast and South, and the 6-week trend still shows growth in SE 46. The bulletin repeats "sinal de crescimento" for COVID-19 nationally.

(f) Adjustment: I start from about 72%. Strongly rising leading indicators and a mechanically sticky long-term trend push me up. Early deceleration in Mato Grosso, small counts and wording risk hold me back. I land around 77%.

Probability: 77%

(a) About 10 days remain. The SE 46 Resumo is expected on 26 November 2026. The question resolves YES if its national highlights or its "Situação nacional" section say that COVID-19 SRAG cases show growth ("sinal de crescimento" or "crescimento") in Brazil as a whole, on either the 6-week or the 3-week trend.

(b) Status quo: the SE 43 and SE 44 editions both reported a national growth signal for COVID-19 SRAG. If nothing changes, the answer is YES.

(c) Base rate: once InfoGripe reports a national virus-specific growth signal during an active wave, it usually persists. I estimate it carries forward two more editions about 65-70% of the time. The main failure mode is a flip to "estabilização" or "oscilação" when the latest weeks flatten after nowcasting.

(d) Evidence for YES:
- The SE 44 edition (12 Nov) reports a national COVID-19 SRAG growth signal.
- COVID-19's share of positive SRAG cases rose from 8.5% to 11.5% between editions, and the number of states with growth went from 5 to 6.
- ITpS test positivity was about 17% in SE 44, the highest since February, up roughly 8 points in a month and still climbing.
- Mild cases are rising in 18 states (Ministry of Health, 10 Nov), with the XFG subvariant dominant.
- Hospitalisations lag infections, so the SRAG rise should continue into late November.
